# dsh-plugin-infinite-split-tabs

Infinite split tabs for the **DeepSeek Harness** right sidebar: split down as well as right,
nest pa
nes in both directions, drag tabs to any edge, and keep every layout across reloads.

> **Status: source patch, not yet a drop-in `dsh plugin add` package.**
> DSH links `ui-dockkit` int

o the Web shell statically, and `ui-sidebar-right` owns the dock.
> A third-party plugin cannot repl

ace that split renderer at runtime, so this repository
> ships the working patch plus the test/build

evidence. See ROADMAP.md for the
> plugin conversion.
## Proposal
Posted in upstream GitHub Discussions (Ideas):
**Split the right sidebar in both directions (nested panes)**
## Review
The source diff is recorded as a draft PR in the contributor's fork:
**jeremytenjo/deepseek-harness#1 — feat(sidebar): split down and unbounded nested panes**

`deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` currently disables external pull requests, so the PR cannot be
opened

against the upstream repository. The fork PR is the reviewable record of the same
24-file change sh
ipped in this repository's `patches/` directory.
## Features

- **Split down** — `⌘⇧\` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+\` on Windows/Linux.
- **Split right** — the existing

`⌘\` still works.
- **Nest both ways** — split any pane again, along either axis; there is no two-p

ane cap.
- **Drag to any edge** — left, right, top or bottom; the drop hint names the target.
- **Pe

rsistent layouts** — the nested split tree is saved per Session and restored.
- **Stable tab bodies*

* — tabs stay siblings in one flat CSS Grid, so terminals and file
previews are not remounted by nes

ting.
- **One-line borders** — every pane on the panel's left edge draws its border, and stacked
pan
es share a single 1px seam (no doubled divider line).

The patch is built against `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` at commit **`22ddee3`**
(the `0.2.1-rc.3`
tree). Use a matching checkout; newer `master` may conflict.

The script runs `git apply --check` first and refuses a dirty/conflicting tree.
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]

At the recorded revision: **542 tests pass**, both packages typecheck, and a live headless
Chrome ru

n built a five-pane nested tree, restored it after reload, and dragged a nested
divider.
## Screenshots
| Stacked + drop hint | Nested tree |
| Single-line seam | 2×2 |
## How it works
The patch touches three layers:

1. `ui-dockkit` — `TabLayout` flattens the split tree into one CSS Grid; each pane maps to
the Grid

tracks its rectangle covers, and each split gets a divider overlay sized to its
own rectangle. `plan

SplitPane`/`DockController` take an axis. The docked-pane ceiling is
removed (`MAX_DOCK_PANES = Infi

nity`).
2. `ui-sidebar-right` — the store/service accept nested splits and top/bottom drops; the
`pa

ne.splitDown` shortcut is registered; persistence validates arbitrary trees.
3. Borders — left-edge
and seam classes replace the old first-column/column-only rules.
## Compatibility and caveats

- Built and tested against DSH **0.2.1-rc.3**.
- The split strip button still splits right; downward

split is the shortcut/API.
- Edge drops use the dock kit's 25% edge bands (all four edges).
- There

is no pane cap, so very deep trees can get cramped; the room rule still refuses a
split when a pane

cannot hold two working halves.
- Stock DSH rejects these nested layouts; downgrading clears that S

ession's stored layout.
- Upstream currently disables external pull requests; this repo is the distr

ed layout.
- Upstream currently disables external pull requests; this repo is the distribution path.
